description: Theorems whose formal verification the project relies on. A fingerprint is set only after the Lean statement has been compared with its source statement; verify_lean.py fails when a statement no longer matches its reviewed fingerprint.

theorems.name: Conjectura.Calibration.sum_range_odd
theorems.source_statement: Classical identity: 1 + 3 + ... + (2n - 1) = n^2 for every natural number n.

theorems.name: Conjectura.Calibration.odd_of_prime_of_two_lt
theorems.source_statement: Classical fact: every prime number greater than 2 is odd.

theorems.name: Conjectura.Research.CollinsShorPeak.maxIndex_ge_iff_pred_lt
theorems.source_statement: research/active/CJ-0001-collins-shor-peak/notes/lemmas.md, R1, 'General form': Let a_0, ..., a_r be positive and log-concave (a_k^2 >= a_{k-1} a_{k+1} for 1 <= k <= r-1) and let 1 <= j <= r. Then every maximizing index of the sequence (an index i <= r with a_i >= a_k for all k <= r) is >= j if and only if a_{j-1} < a_j. Encoding: a : N -> R, only indices <= r constrained; log-concavity written with the middle index shifted by one (equivalent to the literal form by logConcave_shift_iff); a_{j-1} is a (j - 1) under the hypothesis 1 <= j. A supporting lemma of the investigation about finite sequences; it does not mention trees or distance matrices.

theorems.name: Conjectura.Research.CollinsShorPeak.maxIndex_ge_of_pred_lt
theorems.source_statement: One direction of research/active/CJ-0001-collins-shor-peak/notes/lemmas.md, R1, 'General form' (the direction used by the later results): for a_0, ..., a_r positive and log-concave and 1 <= j <= r, if a_{j-1} < a_j then every maximizing index of the sequence is >= j. Same encoding as maxIndex_ge_iff_pred_lt.

theorems.name: Conjectura.Research.CollinsShorPeak.lt_of_pred_lt
theorems.source_statement: Step of the proof of R1, 'General form', in research/active/CJ-0001-collins-shor-peak/notes/lemmas.md ('the sequence is strictly increasing up to j'), in the weaker form that is needed: for a_0, ..., a_r positive and log-concave and 1 <= j <= r, if a_{j-1} < a_j then a_i < a_j for every i < j. Not the 'General form' itself. Same encoding as maxIndex_ge_iff_pred_lt.

theorems.name: Conjectura.Research.CollinsShorPeak.logConcave_shift_iff
theorems.source_statement: Encoding lemma with no counterpart in the notes: for a : N -> R and r, the literal log-concavity condition of R1 'General form' (a_{k-1} a_{k+1} <= a_k^2 for all k with 1 <= k and k + 1 <= r) is equivalent to the shifted condition used as hypothesis in this module (a_k a_{k+2} <= a_{k+1}^2 for all k with k + 2 <= r).

nonvacuity.not_needed: The statement is an equivalence with no hypotheses.

theorems.name: Conjectura.Research.CollinsShorPeak.min_endpoints_le_of_concave
theorems.source_statement: One step of the proof of Lemma L4 ('vertex principle') in research/active/CJ-0001-collins-shor-peak/notes/vertex-principle.md: 'On the interval -(c_i - lambda_i) <= t <= c_k - lambda_k a concave function is at least the smaller of its values at the two ends.' NOT Lemma L4 itself, and a discrete reformulation of that step: for phi : N -> R and N, if phi(t) + phi(t+2) <= 2 phi(t+1) for every t with t + 2 <= N, then min(phi(0), phi(N)) <= phi(t) for every t <= N. Differences from the written step: the function is a real sequence on the integer points 0..N of the interval (the interval is translated so that its left end is 0), and concavity is the non-positivity of second differences at integer points, in place of the concavity of the real quadratic phi(t) = f(c + t(e_i - e_k)), which L4 derives from the non-negativity of the mixed partial derivative d^2 f / dx_i dx_k. No polynomial, no derivative and no multi-affinity appear in the formal statement; that the hypotheses of L4 imply the second-difference hypothesis is not formalized. Encoding: only phi(0..N) is constrained; the middle index is shifted by one to avoid subtraction in N.

theorems.name: Conjectura.Research.CollinsShorPeak.min_vertices_le_of_exchange
theorems.source_statement: The exchange step of the proof of Lemma L4 ('vertex principle') in research/active/CJ-0001-collins-shor-peak/notes/vertex-principle.md, for the two coordinates (i, k) that are moved, all other coordinates being fixed: f(c) >= min(f(c'), f(c'')), where c' and c'' are the two ends of the segment c + t(e_i - e_k) inside {x >= lambda}. NOT Lemma L4 itself (no s variables, no induction on the number of coordinates above their lower bound, no conclusion about the vertices lambda + (S - sum lambda) e_p for s > 2), and a discrete reformulation: for f : Z -> Z -> R and integers a0, b0, S, if f(a+1, b-1) + f(a-1, b+1) <= 2 f(a, b) for all integers a > a0, b > b0 with a + b = S, then min(f(a0, S - a0), f(S - b0, b0)) <= f(a, b) for all integers a >= a0, b >= b0 with a + b = S. Differences from the written lemma: the hypothesis is a second-difference inequality at the integer points of the line a + b = S that are strictly above both lower bounds, in place of 'f is a polynomial of degree at most 1 in each variable whose mixed partial derivative is non-negative at every real point x >= lambda'; for such an f the second difference equals -2 d^2 f / dx_i dx_k <= 0, but that implication is not formalized. The written hypothesis S > sum lambda_i is not assumed (when no point satisfies a >= a0, b >= b0, a + b = S the conclusion is empty; when S = a0 + b0 it is an equality). For s = 2 the conclusion coincides with that of L4 with lambda = (a0, b0).
